svg.title: Super Metroid codebase at Source 0cc905d6a7f4: 114,504 production, 17,793 legacy bank lines, 773 unsafe functions and 620 unsafe blocks
svg.desc: Each row is one responsibility; its number is the production Rust line count. The stacked bar shows the fraction of those lines classified as owned (green), partly owned (amber) or legacy (blue). The three numbers below the bar are their line counts in that order. Rows have equal height; their size does not represent source volume. These are whole-file source classifications, not proof that a subsystem is complete. Owned requires forbid(unsafe_code), no unsafe operations, g_ram, Game or direct foreign calls. Bank files and unsafe files without that marker are legacy; other files are partly owned. The legacy bank headline is only a subset of the blue legacy total. Every area also gives explicit unsafe function and block counts, using production Rust only. Function counts include named unsafe fn declarations, excluding function-pointer types. Block counts include explicit unsafe brace expressions. Comments, ordinary/raw/byte/C strings and character literals are ignored; counts describe source syntax, not macro expansions. Per-area unsafe counts sum exactly to the headlines; verification is excluded. Headline changes compare the source with its state one hour earlier, carried forward from the latest first-parent ancestor. Each small curve samples explicit unsafe blocks in that area at up to nine evenly spaced times over the one hour ending at this staged snapshot, using first-parent committed source and the staged source. Revisions are measured once and shared by all rows. Curves use a local vertical range; lower means fewer blocks. Green segments decrease, red segments increase and gray segments stay level. Sparse commits retain plateaus; no rate is extrapolated. Missing early history is left blank. Samples can miss changes between observations and area reclassification can change counts without removing unsafe code.
